summary: Vaibhav Singh is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology who completed his PhD at the University of Reading in 2017 and held an attested post there in 2018.

Valdo H. Viglielmo (1926–2016) was a scholar of Japanology and philosophy. He studied at UPenn, Harvard, the University of Tokyo, Gakushuin University, and Meiji Gakuin University, and served as a professor at the University of Hawaiʻi (1965–2002).
Valeria Gazizova specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. She studied at the University of Oslo, completing a master's thesis attested in 2009 under the supervision of Per Kværne.

Valerie Stoker works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. She studied under traditional teachers D. Prahladachar and Krishnacharya Tammannacharya Pandurangi, and held a post at Wright State University.
Vamana was an Indologist who studied under traditional teachers Keshava, Dattatreya Sastri Nigudkar, Virupaksha, and Vaidyanātha.
Vamanshastri Kinjawadekar worked in Indology and philosophy, having studied under traditional teachers Dattatreya, Virupaksha, and Vaidyanātha.

Van Austin Harvey (1926–2021) was a religious studies and philosophy scholar. Educated at Occidental College, Princeton Theological Seminary, and Yale University, he held posts at Princeton, Southern Methodist, UPenn, and Stanford (1978–1996).
Vans Kennedy (1784–1846) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He served as judge-advocate-general in the Bombay Army (1817–1835) and as president of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (~1835–1846).

Vasily Mikhaylovich Alekseyev (1881–1951) was a Sinologist who studied at St. Petersburg University and under Édouard Chavannes. He worked at the University of Saint Petersburg (1910–1951) and the Institute of Oriental Studies (1918–1951).

Vasily Pavlovich Vasilyev (1818–1900) was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. Educated at Kazan Federal University under Józef Szczepan Kowalewski, he held professorships at Kazan and the University of Saint Petersburg.

Vasily Radlov (1837–1918) was a linguist, historian, and archaeologist. After studying at the University of Berlin and earning his doctorate at the University of Jena in 1858, he directed the Kunstkamera from 1894 to 1918.

Vasily Seseman (1884–1963) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Saint Petersburg (1903–1909). He held academic posts at Saint Petersburg, Vytautas Magnus University (1923–1940), and Vilnius University (1940–1963).

Vasudev Vishnu Mirashi (1893–1985) was an Indologist and historian educated at Deccan College and the University of Mumbai. He served as principal of Morris College and Vidarbha Institute, and as honorary professor at Nagpur University.

Vasudev Vishwanath Gokhale (1901–1991) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology, earning a PhD from the University of Bonn in 1930. He held professorships at Fergusson College and the University of Delhi.

Vasudeva Sharan Agrawala (1904–1967) was an Indologist and historian educated at Banaras Hindu University and the University of Lucknow. He held posts at the Government Museum in Mathura, State Museum Lucknow, and Banaras Hindu University.

Vasudha Dalmia is an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at Delhi, Cologne, JNU, and Heidelberg. She held positions at Tübingen, JNU, UC Berkeley, Free University of Berlin, and Yale University (2013–2014).

Vasudha Narayanan is a religious studies and Indology scholar educated at Madras, Mumbai, and Harvard universities. She served as Distinguished Professor at the University of Florida from ~1982 and president of the American Academy of Religion (~2001–2002).

Veeranarayana N. K. Pandurangi is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Central Sanskrit University and Rashtriya Sanskrit Vidyapeetha. He held posts at Poornaprajna Vidyapeetha, JR Rajasthan Sanskrit University, and Karnataka Samskrit University.

Velcheru Narayana Rao is an Indologist educated at Sir C.R. Reddy College, Andhra University, and Osmania University. He served as associate professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from 1971 and held visiting professorships at Chicago and Emory.

Vempati Kutumba Sastry is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He served as Vice-Chancellor of Central Sanskrit University (2003–2008) and president of the International Association of Sanskrit Studies (~2006–2018).
